rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. Just cause is either at-fault (e.g., nonpayment, breach, nuisance, criminal activity) or no-fault (owner/relative move-in for 12 months, withdrawal from rental market, government/court orders, demolition or substantial remodel), with no-fault grounds requiring good faith, notice contents and re-offer/relocation obligations.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property with a tenancy of more than 30 days in San Diego, except listed exemptions (including housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years).
rules.exemptions_text: Transient/tourist hotels, short-term occupancy, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under the MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities and transitional housing, dormitories, shared-facility rooms with resident landlord, owner-occupied single-family residences, owner-occupied duplexes, housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, and separately alienable property owned by non-corporate/non-REIT landlords with written notice.

exemption_tests.description: Short-term residential occupancy under Chapter 5, Art. 10, Div. 1 (§98.0703(b))
Housing restricted by deed or agreement as affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income persons (§98.0703(c))
Housing subject to an agreement providing housing subsidies for affordable housing; does not include Section 8 (§98.0703(d))
Mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law (§98.0703(e))
Housing in nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, residential care facility for the elderly, adult residential facility, or non-profit transitional housing (§98.0703(f))
Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or K-12 institution (§98.0703(g))
Tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with landlord who maintains principal residence there (§98.0703(h))
Single-family residence occupied by landlord as principal residence, renting no more than two bedrooms/ADUs/JADUs, or a mobilehome (§98.0703(i))
Property with two dwelling units in a single structure where landlord occupies one as principal residence at start of tenancy (§98.0703(j))
Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless a mobilehome (§98.0703(k))

Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit, where landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and tenants were given written exemption notice (§98.0703(l))

rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; at-fault and no-fault grounds
rules.ambiguity_note: Section 98.0704 amended 2-27-2024, effective 3-28-2024. Remedies, relocation assistance (§98.0706) continue in the next chunk.
